header.system:
You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are the integrating analyst of a code-safety review. Six departments have each committed `findings/<department>.json` and `report/<department>.md` on their own branch, and this worktree is the merge of all of them. You write two files and nothing else: `findings.json` and `SAFETY-REPORT.md`.

Read `REPORTING.md` in this worktree first: it states the finding format, the exact sections of the report, the count lines both summaries carry, and the certificate's wording. Read `target.json` for the tree under review and the SHA-256 the certificate states. Read every `findings/*.json` and every `report/*.md` before writing anything. When a `report-template` skill is available, load it: it owns how the report reads, while `REPORTING.md` owns what the examiner mechanically decides and wins wherever the two differ in form.

Ask the examiner which findings do not hold before you write the union:

    for f in findings/*.json; do node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings "$f" --list-invalid; done

Every id it prints is dropped from `findings.json` and named under `## What was not covered`, with the reason. Dropping one silently fails the report.

`findings.json` is the union, deduplicated by `file` plus `line` plus `cwe`, keeping the entry whose `confidence` is higher. Copy each entry whole; do not rewrite a department's `snippet`, because the examiner compares it with the target's own text.

The report is a review by a language model, grounded by a static scanner and by the committed examiner, over the files the departments actually read. `## Scope and method` says that, names the departments that ran and the tools that ran, and states what was read rather than what exists. `## What was not covered` is not a formality: name the file kinds nobody opened, the classes of defect no department owns, the checks that did not run, and every dropped finding. Never write that the target is secure, safe or free of vulnerabilities — nothing this program did could support it, and the examiner refuses the claim.

Before you stop, run `node verify-safety-report.mjs --report`, fix every line it names, and commit everything. Work left uncommitted is not delivered and is not measured. Never write into the target tree, and never edit `verify-safety-report.mjs`, `target.json` or any department's committed files.


Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one is sampled across top-level entries, so it spans the tree instead of one subtree.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result instead returns 100 paths sampled across top-level entries, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

1: # How this program reports what it found
2: 
3: This worktree is the **report repository**. The code under review is the **target tree**, which is somewhere else on this host: `target.json` beside this file states its absolute path, the files it covers, and the SHA-256 the whole tree locks to.
4: 
5: The target is read-only for every session of this program. `verify-safety-report.mjs` re-hashes every locked file on every run, so a target a department edited fails the program instead of releasing a report about a tree that no longer exists.
6: 
7: ## This file and the skills
8: 
9: When the deployment mounts the code-safety knowledge pack, its `review-method`, `severity-and-evidence` and `report-template` skills own the craft: how to read a codebase, how to score a severity, what evidence has to name, and how the report reads. Follow them.
10: 
11: This file owns what `verify-safety-report.mjs` mechanically decides, and it is binding wherever the two differ in form. There is one such place and it is stated below: the counts each summary carries are written as `- <severity>: <count>` lines so the examiner can compare them with the union, which is the machine-readable form of the skill's "counts per severity".
12: 
13: ## What a department delivers
14: 
15: Two files, both committed on the department's own branch:
16: 
17: - `findings/<department>.json` — a JSON array of findings, `[]` when the department found nothing.
18: - `report/<department>.md` — the department's own prose: what it looked at, what it found, and what it did not reach.
19: 
20: Nothing else. Do not write `SAFETY-REPORT.md`, `findings.json`, `target.json` or `verify-safety-report.mjs`: the first two are the integration's, and the last two are the examiner.
21: 
22: ## The evidence rule
23: 
24: A finding without a file and a line is not a finding. Quote the exact line you cite; `verify-safety-report.mjs` compares your `snippet` with the target's own text at that line, ignoring only whitespace, and refuses the whole file when they differ.
25: 
26: Prefer three findings you have read the code for over twelve a pattern matched. `confidence` is what you actually know: `confirmed` when you read the sink, the source and the path between them; `likely` when the sink is dangerous and the source is plausibly attacker-controlled; `possible` when the pattern is there and the reachability is not established.
27: 
28: ## The finding
29: 
30: ```json
31: {
32:   "id": "secrets-cookie-secret",
33:   "cwe": "CWE-798",
34:   "owasp": "A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures",
35:   "severity": "high",
36:   "confidence": "confirmed",
37:   "title": "Session cookie secret is hard-coded in the committed configuration",
38:   "file": "config/env/all.js",
39:   "line": 8,
40:   "snippet": "cookieSecret: \"session_cookie_secret_key_here\",",
41:   "evidence": "The value is a literal in a committed file and is the secret express-session is configured with.",
42:   "impact": "Anyone with the repository can forge a session cookie and authenticate as any user.",
43:   "fix": "Read the secret from the environment and rotate the committed value.",
44:   "references": ["https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html"]
45: }
46: ```
47: 
48: | Field | Rule |
49: | --- | --- |
50: | `id` | letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores, unique across the whole program; prefix it with your department or use the pack's `SEC-<n>` numbering. |
51: | `cwe` | `CWE-<number>`. |
52: | `owasp` | the OWASP Top 10 category, named. |
53: | `severity` | `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low` or `info`. |
54: | `confidence` | `confirmed`, `likely` or `possible`. |
55: | `title` | one line a reader can act on. |
56: | `file` | path relative to the target root, exactly as `target.json` lists it. |
57: | `line` | 1-based line in that file. |
58: | `endLine` | optional last line when the finding spans several; `snippet` then quotes all of them. |

The target is read-only for every session of this program. `verify-safety-report.mjs` re-hashes every locked file on every run, so a target a department edited fails the program instead of releasing a report about a tree that no longer exists.

This file owns what `verify-safety-report.mjs` mechanically decides, and it is binding wherever the two differ in form. There is one such place and it is stated below: the counts each summary carries are written as `- <severity>: <count>` lines so the examiner can compare them with the union, which is the machine-readable form of the skill's "counts per severity".
Two files, both committed on the department's own branch:
- `findings/<department>.json` — a JSON array of findings, `[]` when the department found nothing.
- `report/<department>.md` — the department's own prose: what it looked at, what it found, and what it did not reach.

<skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>
# The report layout

Every report has exactly these sections, in this order. Do not add marketing language, severity totals presented as a score out of ten, or a remediation timeline the review has no authority to commit the customer to.

- **`## Résumé exécutif`** — French. Counts per severity, the three most important findings by name and effect, what was and was not covered in one sentence each, and one paragraph on method.
- **`## Executive summary`** — the same content in English, for a mixed-language or non-French reader.
- **`## Scope and method`** — the repository, commit or tag reviewed, which directories or services were in scope, and a link to [review-method](../review-method/SKILL.md).
- **`## Findings`** — grouped by severity, critical first; one bullet per finding with its id, title, `file:line`, CWE, and confidence. Full detail (snippet, evidence, impact, fix) lives in the accompanying JSON per [severity-and-evidence](../severity-and-evidence/SKILL.md), not duplicated in prose here.
- **`## What was not covered`** — the [review-method](../review-method/SKILL.md) not-covered list, specific to this engagement.
- **`## Certificate`** — what a mechanical verifier checked after the fact: every finding resolves to a real file and line in the reviewed commit, every id is unique, every CWE/OWASP id is a known identifier, and no two findings share file, line, and CWE. This certifies the report's internal consistency, not the completeness or correctness of the review's judgment.

## Filled example: a small Express app

```markdown
## Résumé exécutif

Cette revue a porté sur le code source de commande-api, une application Express.js
de gestion de commandes, au commit a1b2c3d. Elle a permis d'identifier 3 constats :
1 critique, 1 moyen et 1 faible. Les plus importants : (1) une injection SQL
critique dans la recherche de commande par identifiant (src/routes/orders.js:42),
permettant de lire ou modifier toute donnée accessible par l'utilisateur de base de
données de l'application ; (2) une fixation de session lors de la connexion
(src/routes/auth.js:58) ; (3) l'absence de l'en-tête HSTS (src/app.js:12). La revue
a couvert les points d'entrée HTTP, l'authentification et la gestion des sessions ;
elle n'a pas couvert l'infrastructure de déploiement ni les dépendances tierces
(voir « Ce qui n'a pas été couvert »). Méthode : lecture des points d'entrée,
suivi des données de la source jusqu'au point d'exécution, un constat par point
d'exécution, ligne exactement citée et niveau de confiance déclaré pour chacun.

## Executive summary

This review covered commande-api, an Express.js order-management application, at
commit a1b2c3d, and found 3 issues: 1 critical, 1 medium, 1 low. The most
important: (1) a critical SQL injection in order lookup by id
(src/routes/orders.js:42); (2) session fixation on login
(src/routes/auth.js:58); (3) a missing HSTS header (src/app.js:12). HTTP entry
points, authentication, and session handling were covered; deployment
infrastructure and third-party dependencies were not (see "What was not covered").

## Scope and method

Repository commande-api, commit a1b2c3d, `src/` only. Method: [review-method](../review-method/SKILL.md).

## Findings

### Critical
- SEC-001 — SQL injection in order lookup — `src/routes/orders.js:42` — CWE-89 — confirmed

### Medium
- SEC-002 — Session id not rotated after login (session fixation) — `src/routes/auth.js:58` — CWE-384 — likely

### Low
- SEC-003 — Missing Strict-Transport-Security header — `src/app.js:12` — CWE-319 — confirmed

## What was not covered

- `infra/` (Terraform, Dockerfiles) and CI/CD configuration.
- Third-party dependency advisories (separate engagement).
- Runtime configuration: actual deployed environment variables, WAF rules, and network topology.
- Native mobile or memory-safety classes of bug: this codebase has no native module.

## Certificate

Mechanically verified: 3/3 findings resolve to an existing line at commit a1b2c3d;
3/3 ids unique; 3/3 CWE and OWASP ids recognized; 0 findings share file, line, and
CWE. This certifies internal consistency only, not completeness of coverage.
```
</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: // Mechanical examiner of a code-safety report. It is in the report
3: // repository's base commit, so no department can change what measures it.
4: //
5: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <path>  one department's findings
6: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <path> --list-invalid
7: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --report           the merged report
8: //
9: // `--findings` decides one findings file against the target tree. Adding
10: // `--list-invalid` turns the same decision into a report: the failing ids go to
11: // stdout, one per line, and the exit code is 0, which is how the integration
12: // learns which findings to drop and disclose.
13: //
14: // `--report` decides SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json together, including the
15: // disclosure rule: every id any `findings/<department>.json` carries and
16: // findings.json does not must be named under `## What was not covered`.
17: //
18: // Exit 0 only when every rule holds; otherwise every failure is printed to
19: // stderr, one per line, and the exit code is 1. Node built-ins only, because
20: // this runs in a worktree that installs nothing.
21: import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
22: import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
23: import { basename, join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
24: 
25: /** Severities a finding may claim, most severe first. */
26: const SEVERITIES = ['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low', 'info']
27: 
28: /** How sure a finding's author is that the cited code is exploitable as described. */
29: const CONFIDENCES = ['confirmed', 'likely', 'possible']
30: 
31: /** Sections SAFETY-REPORT.md carries, in this order. */
32: const SECTIONS = [
33:   '## Résumé exécutif',
34:   '## Executive summary',
35:   '## Scope and method',
36:   '## Findings',
37:   '## What was not covered',
38:   '## Certificate',
39: ]
40: 
41: /** The claim the certificate must make verbatim, and the only claim this review supports. */
42: const HONESTY = 'This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".'
43: 
44: /** Claims no coverage this review can state would support. */
45: const OVERCLAIMS = /\bno vulnerabilities\b|\bfree of vulnerabilities\b|\b(?:is|are|was|were) secure\b|\bsafe to deploy\b|\bproven secure\b|\bfully audited\b/i
46: 
47: /** Text a report still carrying its template is refused for. */
48: const PLACEHOLDER = /\bTODO\b|\bTBD\b|\bFIXME\b|lorem ipsum|<placeholder>|PLACEHOLDER/i
49: 
50: /** String fields every finding states in prose. */
51: const PROSE_FIELDS = ['title', 'evidence', 'impact', 'fix']
52: 
53: /** How a file's text is compared with a finding's quoted snippet. */
54: const normalize = (text) => text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()
55: 
56: /** Lowercase hex SHA-256 of one buffer or string. */
57: const sha256 = (content) => createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
58: 
59: /**
60:  * Every file under one directory, relative and sorted, skipping the excluded names.
61:  * @param {string} root directory to walk
62:  * @param {string[]} exclude directory basenames never descended into
63:  * @returns {string[]} relative POSIX-ish paths, sorted
64:  */
65: function walk(root, exclude) {
66:   const found = []
67:   const descend = (directory) => {
68:     for (const entry of readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
69:       const path = join(directory, entry.name)
70:       if (entry.isDirectory()) {
71:         if (!exclude.includes(entry.name)) descend(path)
72:       } else if (entry.isFile()) found.push(relative(root, path))
73:     }
74:   }
75:   descend(root)
76:   return found.sort()
77: }
78: 
79: /** One target tree as the lock and the verifier both read it: the files, their digests, and their text. */
80: class Target {
81:   /**
82:    * @param {string} reportRoot the report repository the lock is committed in
83:    * @param {string[]} failures collector every rule appends to
84:    */
85:   constructor(reportRoot, failures) {
86:     this.failures = failures
87:     this.root = undefined
88:     this.files = new Map()
89:     this.lines = new Map()
90:     const lockPath = join(reportRoot, 'target.json')
91:     if (!existsSync(lockPath)) {
92:       failures.push('target.json is missing from this worktree; the base commit carries the lock of the tree under review')
93:       return
94:     }
95:     const lock = JSON.parse(readFileSync(lockPath, 'utf8'))
96:     this.root = lock.root
97:     this.exclude = lock.exclude ?? []
98:     this.digest = lock.sha256
99:     for (const [path, hash] of Object.entries(lock.files)) this.files.set(path, hash)
100:     this.checkTree()
101:   }
102: 
103:   /**
104:    * Refuse a target that changed since the base commit locked it: a finding
105:    * cites a line of the tree this program was asked to review, and a tree a
106:    * department edited is no longer that tree.
107:    */
108:   checkTree() {
109:     if (!existsSync(this.root)) {
110:       this.failures.push(`the target tree ${this.root} is not on this host, so no citation can be resolved`)
111:       this.root = undefined
112:       return
113:     }
114:     const present = walk(this.root, this.exclude)
115:     for (const path of present) {
116:       if (!this.files.has(path)) this.failures.push(`the target tree gained ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
117:     }
118:     for (const [path, hash] of this.files) {
119:       if (!present.includes(path)) {
120:         this.failures.push(`the target tree lost ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
121:         continue
122:       }
123:       if (sha256(readFileSync(join(this.root, path))) !== hash) {
124:         this.failures.push(`the target tree's ${path} changed since the base commit locked it; the target is read-only for this program`)
125:       }
126:     }
127:   }
128: 
129:   /**
130:    * The lines of one target file.
131:    * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
132:    * @returns {string[] | undefined} the file's lines, or undefined when it is not in the locked tree
133:    */
134:   linesOf(path) {
135:     if (this.root === undefined || !this.files.has(path)) return undefined
136:     if (!this.lines.has(path)) this.lines.set(path, readFileSync(join(this.root, path), 'utf8').split('\n'))
137:     return this.lines.get(path)
138:   }
139: 
140:   /**
141:    * Whether one `file:line` citation resolves in the locked tree.
142:    * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
143:    * @param {number} line 1-based line number
144:    * @returns {boolean} whether the file is under review and holds that line
145:    */
146:   resolves(path, line) {
147:     const lines = this.linesOf(path)
148:     return lines !== undefined && Number.isInteger(line) && line >= 1 && line <= lines.length
149:   }
150: }
151: 
152: /**
153:  * Decide one finding against the target tree.
154:  * @param {unknown} finding one entry of a findings file
155:  * @param {number} index its position, named when the entry has no usable id
156:  * @param {Target} target the locked tree the finding cites
157:  * @param {Set<string>} seen ids already used in this file
158:  * @returns {string[]} every rule this finding broke, empty when it holds
159:  */
160: function checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen) {
161:   const failures = []
162:   if (finding === null || typeof finding !== 'object' || Array.isArray(finding)) {
163:     return [`finding #${index + 1} is not a JSON object`]
164:   }
165:   const id = finding.id
166:   const name = typeof id === 'string' && id !== '' ? id : `#${index + 1}`
167:   const fail = (rule) => void failures.push(`${name}: ${rule}`)
168:   // Letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`: wide enough for both the `SEC-001`
169:   // numbering the knowledge pack's schema uses and a department-prefixed name.
170:   if (typeof id !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$/.test(id)) fail('id must be letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores')
171:   else if (seen.has(id)) fail('id is used twice in this file')
172:   else seen.add(id)
173:   if (typeof finding.cwe !== 'string' || !/^CWE-\d+$/.test(finding.cwe)) fail('cwe must match CWE-<number>')
174:   if (typeof finding.owasp !== 'string' || finding.owasp.trim() === '') fail('owasp must name the category')
175:   if (!SEVERITIES.includes(finding.severity)) fail(`severity must be one of ${SEVERITIES.join(', ')}`)
176:   if (!CONFIDENCES.includes(finding.confidence)) fail(`confidence must be one of ${CONFIDENCES.join(', ')}`)
177:   for (const field of PROSE_FIELDS) {
178:     if (typeof finding[field] !== 'string' || finding[field].trim() === '') fail(`${field} must be a non-empty string`)
179:   }
180:   if (!Array.isArray(finding.references) || finding.references.some(reference => typeof reference !== 'string')) {
181:     fail('references must be an array of strings')
182:   }
183:   const { file, line, endLine, snippet } = finding
184:   if (typeof file !== 'string' || file === '' || file.startsWith('/') || file.split('/').includes('..')) {
185:     fail('file must be a path relative to the target root')
186:     return failures
187:   }
188:   const lines = target.linesOf(file)
189:   if (lines === undefined) {
190:     fail(`file ${file} is not in the tree under review`)
191:     return failures
192:   }
193:   if (!Number.isInteger(line) || line < 1 || line > lines.length) {
194:     fail(`line ${JSON.stringify(line)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
195:     return failures
196:   }
197:   const last = endLine === undefined ? line : endLine
198:   if (!Number.isInteger(last) || last < line || last > lines.length) {
199:     fail(`endLine ${JSON.stringify(endLine)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
200:     return failures
201:   }
202:   if (typeof snippet !== 'string' || snippet.trim() === '') {
203:     fail('snippet must quote the cited line')
204:     return failures
205:   }
206:   const quoted = normalize(lines.slice(line - 1, last).join('\n'))
207:   if (normalize(snippet) !== quoted) {
208:     fail(`snippet does not match ${file}:${line}, which reads ${JSON.stringify(quoted.slice(0, 160))}`)
209:   }
210:   return failures
211: }
212: 
213: /**
214:  * Read one findings file.
215:  * @param {string} path the file to read
216:  * @param {string[]} failures collector a malformed file is reported on
217:  * @returns {unknown[]} the entries, empty when the file is missing or malformed
218:  */
219: function readFindings(path, failures) {
220:   if (!existsSync(path)) {
221:     failures.push(`${path} is missing`)
222:     return []
223:   }
224:   let parsed
225:   try {
226:     parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'))
227:   } catch (error) {
228:     failures.push(`${path} is not JSON: ${error.message}`)
229:     return []
230:   }
231:   if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) {
232:     failures.push(`${path} must be a JSON array of findings`)
233:     return []
234:   }
235:   return parsed
236: }
237: 
238: /**
239:  * Decide one findings file on its own.
240:  * @param {string} path the findings file
241:  * @param {Target} target the locked tree it cites
242:  * @returns {{ failures: string[], invalid: string[], findings: unknown[] }} the broken rules, the ids that broke them, and the entries
243:  */
244: function checkFindingsFile(path, target) {
245:   const failures = []
246:   const findings = readFindings(path, failures)
247:   const invalid = []
248:   const seen = new Set()
249:   findings.forEach((finding, index) => {
250:     const broken = checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen)
251:     if (broken.length === 0) return
252:     failures.push(...broken.map(rule => `${basename(path)}: ${rule}`))
253:     invalid.push(typeof finding?.id === 'string' ? finding.id : `#${index + 1}`)
254:   })
255:   return { failures, invalid, findings }
256: }
257: 
258: /**
259:  * The body of one section of the report.
260:  * @param {string} text the whole report
261:  * @param {string} heading the section heading, including its `##`
262:  * @returns {string} the text between this heading and the next one, empty when absent
263:  */
264: function section(text, heading) {
265:   const start = text.indexOf(`${heading}\n`)
266:   if (start === -1) return ''
267:   const body = text.slice(start + heading.length + 1)
268:   const next = body.search(/^## /m)
269:   return next === -1 ? body : body.slice(0, next)
270: }
271: 
272: /**
273:  * Decide SAFETY-REPORT.md, findings.json and the disclosure of what was dropped.
274:  * @param {string} root the report repository
275:  * @param {Target} target the locked tree the report cites
276:  * @returns {string[]} every rule the report broke
277:  */
278: function checkReport(root, target) {
279:   const reportPath = join(root, 'SAFETY-REPORT.md')
280:   if (!existsSync(reportPath)) {
281:     return [`SAFETY-REPORT.md is missing; REPORTING.md in this worktree states the sections it carries: ${SECTIONS.join(', ')}`]
282:   }
283:   const text = readFileSync(reportPath, 'utf8')
284:   const failures = []
285:   let previous = -1
286:   for (const heading of SECTIONS) {
287:     const at = text.indexOf(`${heading}\n`)
288:     if (at === -1) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has no section ${JSON.stringify(heading)}`)
289:     else if (at < previous) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has ${JSON.stringify(heading)} out of order; the order is ${SECTIONS.join(' then ')}`)
290:     else previous = at
291:   }
292:   const placeholder = PLACEHOLDER.exec(text)
293:   if (placeholder !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md still carries placeholder text: ${JSON.stringify(placeholder[0])}`)
294:   const overclaim = OVERCLAIMS.exec(text)
295:   if (overclaim !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md claims more than this review supports: ${JSON.stringify(overclaim[0])}`)
296: 
297:   const union = checkFindingsFile(join(root, 'findings.json'), target)
298:   failures.push(...union.failures)
299:   const findings = union.findings.filter(finding => typeof finding?.id === 'string')
300: 
301:   const keys = new Set()
302:   for (const finding of findings) {
303:     const key = `${finding.file}:${finding.line}:${finding.cwe}`
304:     if (keys.has(key)) failures.push(`findings.json states ${key} twice; the union is deduplicated by file, line and cwe`)
305:     keys.add(key)
306:   }
307: 
308:   const listed = section(text, '## Findings')
309:   for (const finding of findings) {
310:     if (!listed.includes(finding.id)) failures.push(`the Findings section does not cite ${finding.id}`)

// repository's base commit, so no department can change what measures it.
// `--findings` decides one findings file against the target tree. Adding
// `--list-invalid` turns the same decision into a report: the failing ids go to
// stdout, one per line, and the exit code is 0, which is how the integration
// learns which findings to drop and disclose.
// `--report` decides SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json together, including the
// disclosure rule: every id any `findings/<department>.json` carries and
// findings.json does not must be named under `## What was not covered`.
// Exit 0 only when every rule holds; otherwise every failure is printed to
// stderr, one per line, and the exit code is 1. Node built-ins only, because
// this runs in a worktree that installs nothing.

/** Severities a finding may claim, most severe first. */
/** How sure a finding's author is that the cited code is exploitable as described. */
/** Sections SAFETY-REPORT.md carries, in this order. */
/** The claim the certificate must make verbatim, and the only claim this review supports. */

const HONESTY = 'This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".'
/** Claims no coverage this review can state would support. */
const OVERCLAIMS = /\bno vulnerabilities\b|\bfree of vulnerabilities\b|\b(?:is|are|was|were) secure\b|\bsafe to deploy\b|\bproven secure\b|\bfully audited\b/i

/** String fields every finding states in prose. */
/** How a file's text is compared with a finding's quoted snippet. */

* @param {string} reportRoot the report repository the lock is committed in
* @param {string[]} failures collector every rule appends to
failures.push('target.json is missing from this worktree; the base commit carries the lock of the tree under review')
for (const [path, hash] of Object.entries(lock.files)) this.files.set(path, hash)
* Refuse a target that changed since the base commit locked it: a finding
* cites a line of the tree this program was asked to review, and a tree a
* department edited is no longer that tree.

if (!this.files.has(path)) this.failures.push(`the target tree gained ${path} since the base commit locked it`)

// Letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`: wide enough for both the `SEC-001`
// numbering the knowledge pack's schema uses and a department-prefixed name.
if (typeof id !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$/.test(id)) fail('id must be letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores')

if (typeof finding.cwe !== 'string' || !/^CWE-\d+$/.test(finding.cwe)) fail('cwe must match CWE-<number>')

if (!SEVERITIES.includes(finding.severity)) fail(`severity must be one of ${SEVERITIES.join(', ')}`)

if (typeof finding[field] !== 'string' || finding[field].trim() === '') fail(`${field} must be a non-empty string`)
fail('references must be an array of strings')
const { file, line, endLine, snippet } = finding
fail('file must be a path relative to the target root')
fail(`file ${file} is not in the tree under review`)

fail(`endLine ${JSON.stringify(endLine)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
fail('snippet must quote the cited line')
fail(`snippet does not match ${file}:${line}, which reads ${JSON.stringify(quoted.slice(0, 160))}`)

failures.push(`${path} must be a JSON array of findings`)
* Decide one findings file on its own.
* @param {Target} target the locked tree it cites

const broken = checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen)
* The body of one section of the report.

return [`SAFETY-REPORT.md is missing; REPORTING.md in this worktree states the sections it carries: ${SECTIONS.join(', ')}`]
else if (at < previous) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has ${JSON.stringify(heading)} out of order; the order is ${SECTIONS.join(' then ')}`)
if (placeholder !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md still carries placeholder text: ${JSON.stringify(placeholder[0])}`)

// the host is preceded by a slash, so no citation ever starts there.
if (!target.resolves(path, Number(line))) failures.push(`the citation ${path}:${line} does not resolve in the tree under review`)
for (const heading of ['## Résumé exécutif', '## Executive summary']) {
if (stated === null) failures.push(`${heading} does not state a "- ${severity}: <count>" line`)
const uncovered = section(text, '## What was not covered')
for (const finding of readFindings(join(department, entry), failures)) {
failures.push(`${id} was dropped from findings.json and is not disclosed under "## What was not covered"`)
if (!certificate.includes(HONESTY)) failures.push(`the Certificate must state, verbatim: ${JSON.stringify(HONESTY)}`)
if (stated === null) failures.push('the Certificate does not state a "Verified findings: <count>" line')
else if (Number(stated[1]) !== findings.length) failures.push(`the Certificate states ${stated[1]} verified findings, and findings.json holds ${findings.length}`)
if (tree === null) failures.push('the Certificate does not state a "Target tree: <sha256>" line')

lines.text: "title": "express is a vulnerable 4.x release pulling six vulnerable transitive packages",

"evidence": "package-lock.json resolves this range to express@4.16.4. `npm audit --json` run in the target (registry reachable; auditReportVersion 2, 1479 resolved dependencies) reports express as vulnerable at range <=4.21.2, with two advisories against express itself -- GHSA-qw6h-vgh9-j6wx (XSS via response.redirect(), CWE-79, fixed <4.20.0) and GHSA-rv95-896h-c2vc (open redirect on malformed URLs, CWE-601/1286, fixed <4.19.2) -- plus 6 transitive vulnerable packages pulled in through this one dependency: body-parser, cookie, path-to-regexp, qs, send and serve-static (qs alone carries 5 distinct prototype-pollution/DoS advisories). express is required directly at server.js:3 and is the core framework handling every route.",

"impact": "An attacker can redirect users to attacker-controlled hosts, inject markup via response.redirect(), or trigger denial-of-service through the vulnerable transitive qs/path-to-regexp parsers -- reachable on every request the framework handles, unauthenticated.",

"fix": "Update express to >=4.21.2 (still within the declared ^4.13.4 range; `npm audit fix` reports a fix is available without a manifest change) and regenerate package-lock.json so the transitive body-parser/cookie/qs/send/serve-static versions are refreshed too.",
"title": "body-parser is pinned to a range that resolves to a version with two denial-of-service advisories",

"evidence": "package-lock.json resolves this range to body-parser@1.18.3. `npm audit --json` reports it vulnerable at range <=1.20.5 with GHSA-qwcr-r2fm-qrc7 (DoS when URL encoding is enabled, CWE-405, fixed >=1.20.3) and GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6 (an invalid `limit` value silently disables size enforcement, CWE-770, fixed >=1.20.6), plus the transitive `qs` package it depends on. body-parser is wired in directly at server.js:5 and used on every incoming request via app.use(bodyParser.json()) and app.use(bodyParser.urlencoded(...)) at server.js:71-75.",
"impact": "An unauthenticated remote attacker can send a crafted request body to exhaust event-loop time or bypass the configured body-size limit, denying service to the whole application.",
"fix": "Update body-parser to >=1.20.6 (within the declared ^1.15.1 range; npm audit reports a non-breaking fix is available) and regenerate the lockfile.",
"title": "marked is pinned to an exact, years-old version with active XSS and ReDoS advisories, and is wired into templates",

"evidence": "The manifest pins the exact version 0.3.5 with no caret, so npm install always resolves this same build; package-lock.json confirms marked@0.3.5 is what installs. `npm audit --json` lists six advisories against this range: GHSA-7px7-7xjx-hxm8 and GHSA-vfvf-mqq8-rwqc (XSS via data URIs / HTML-entity sanitization bypass, CWE-79, both fixed well before 0.3.9), and GHSA-x5pg-88wf-qq4p, GHSA-p9wx-2529-fp83, GHSA-rrrm-qjm4-v8hf, GHSA-5v2h-r2cx-5xgj (regular-expression denial of service, CWE-400/1333, the last two only fixed at >=4.0.10). marked is required at server.js:13, configured with `marked.setOptions({ sanitize: true })` at server.js:126-128 -- the `sanitize` option this exact version relies on is one of the mechanisms the XSS advisories bypass -- and exposed to templates as `app.locals.marked` at server.js:129, i.e. it renders user-submitted markdown (the memos feature) directly into HTML.",

"impact": "A user who can submit markdown content (e.g. via the memos feature) can bypass marked's sanitize option and inject script that executes in another user's session, or trigger a ReDoS that stalls the single Node.js event loop for every request.",

"fix": "At minimum update to marked@0.3.19 (the non-major fix npm audit resolves within this branch); for a durable fix, migrate off the deprecated `sanitize` option entirely and run output through a maintained HTML sanitizer (e.g. DOMPurify) on a current marked major version.",
"title": "swig, the active template engine, is deprecated/unmaintained and has an unfixed arbitrary local file read advisory",

"evidence": "package-lock.json resolves this to swig@1.4.2, the last version swig ever published. `npm view swig deprecated` (registry reachable) returns 'This package is no longer maintained', last modified 2022-06-27. `npm audit --json` reports GHSA-2rq5-699j-x7p6, arbitrary local file read during template rendering (CWE-22, range <=1.4.2, i.e. every published version), with fixAvailable: false -- there is no patched release to move to. swig is required at server.js:9, registered as the view engine via `app.engine('.html', consolidate.swig)` at server.js:116, and explicitly configured with `swig.setDefaults({ autoescape: false })` at server.js:135-137, so the engine that renders every .html view in this app both disables autoescaping and ships an unpatchable file-read bug.",

"impact": "Combined with any template-injection path, an attacker can read arbitrary files on the server filesystem; there is no upstream fix and the maintainers have stopped shipping one, so this risk is permanent as long as swig stays in the dependency tree.",

"fix": "Replace swig with a maintained template engine (the project already loads templates through `consolidate`, which supports several current engines), and re-enable autoescaping in whatever engine replaces it.",
"title": "underscore is pinned to a range resolving to a version with a known arbitrary-code-execution advisory",

"evidence": "package-lock.json resolves this range to underscore@1.9.1. `npm audit --json` reports GHSA-cf4h-3jhx-xvhq, arbitrary code execution via the `_.template` function (CWE-94, range >=1.3.2 <1.12.1 -- 1.9.1 is inside it), and GHSA-qpx9-hpmf-5gmw, unlimited recursion in `_.flatten`/`_.isEqual` leading to DoS (CWE-674/770, range <=1.13.7). `npm view underscore version` shows the current release is 1.13.8, which is outside both vulnerable ranges. underscore is required directly at config/config.js:1.",

"impact": "If `_.template` is ever called with attacker-influenced template source or options, an attacker can execute arbitrary code in the Node.js process; independently, a crafted deeply-nested object handed to `_.flatten` or `_.isEqual` can crash the process via stack exhaustion.",
"fix": "Update underscore to >=1.13.8 and confirm no code path in the application passes attacker-controlled strings into `_.template`.",
"title": "mongodb driver is pinned to an ancient 2.x range with a DoS advisory and an unmaintained transitive driver-core",

"evidence": "package-lock.json resolves this range to mongodb@2.2.36 -- the mongodb Node.js driver's 2.x line, whose latest release (`npm view mongodb version`) is now 7.6.0, five majors ahead. `npm audit --json` reports GHSA-mh5c-679w-hh4r, a denial-of-service in mongodb (range <3.1.13), plus the transitive `mongodb-core` package (itself pulling a vulnerable `bson`). mongodb is required at server.js:11 and used to open the application's only database connection via `MongoClient.connect(db, ...)` at server.js:30.",

"impact": "A malformed server response or crafted query result can crash or hang the database connection layer that every route in the application depends on; the 2.x driver also predates years of TLS, authentication and query-hardening fixes shipped in later majors.",
"fix": "At minimum update to mongodb >=3.1.13 to clear the known DoS; plan a migration to a current major (7.x) since the 2.x line is long past any security support window.",
"title": "forever, a production dependency, pulls four vulnerable transitive packages including a prototype-pollution advisory in nconf",

"impact": "forever itself is not on the HTTP request path, so the realistic exploitation route is through whatever configuration files or environment forever's own tooling parses via nconf; a prototype-pollution there could corrupt process-wide object behavior for anything else sharing the process.",

"title": "bcrypt-nodejs, the password-hashing library, is an npm-flagged deprecated package with no further releases",

"title": "node-esapi, used for output encoding, has had a single release since 2014 and no maintenance since",

lines.text: "title": "NoSQL injection via unsanitized threshold in MongoDB $where clause",

"evidence": "app/routes/allocations.js reads `threshold` straight from `req.query` (const { threshold } = req.query;) at its line 20 and passes it unmodified as the second argument to allocationsDAO.getByUserIdAndThreshold. That function (app/data/allocations-dao.js:57-84) interpolates the raw `threshold` string directly into a MongoDB `$where` JavaScript expression at line 78 with no validation, quoting escape or type coercion (the commented-out block above it, lines 63-76, is the disabled fix that used to call parseInt and range-check the value). The resulting object is passed straight to `allocationsCol.find(searchCriteria())` at line 86, so MongoDB evaluates the attacker's string as server-side JavaScript inside `$where`.",

"impact": "An attacker can submit GET /allocations/<userId>?threshold=' ; while(true){} // or an operator such as 0' ; return true; var x='0 to run arbitrary JavaScript inside the MongoDB server, causing denial of service or bypassing the intended filter to read every user's allocation data.",

"fix": "Never build a $where clause from request input. Validate `threshold` as a bounded integer (parseInt with a 0-99 range check, as the commented-out original fix does) and use a plain query object such as { userId: parsedUserId, stocks: { $gt: parsedThreshold } } instead of a $where string.",
"title": "Server-side JavaScript injection via eval() on contribution percentage (preTax)",

"evidence": "handleContributionsUpdate (app/routes/contributions.js:28) is mounted at POST /contributions with only the isLoggedIn guard (app/routes/index.js:52); no other middleware inspects the body. `req.body.preTax` is passed directly into Node's `eval()` at line 32 with no parsing, type-check or sanitization before or after the call; the only validation (isNaN/negative checks at line 47) runs after eval has already executed.",

"impact": "Any authenticated user can submit a POST /contributions request with preTax set to arbitrary JavaScript (e.g. `require('child_process').execSync('id')` or a process-crashing payload) and have it executed in the Node process, giving full server-side code execution under the application's privileges.",
"fix": "Never eval request data. Parse the value with Number()/parseInt() and reject non-numeric input, as the commented-out fix in the same file (lines 37-40) already shows.",
"title": "Server-side JavaScript injection via eval() on contribution percentage (afterTax)",

"evidence": "Same handler and route as the preTax finding: `req.body.afterTax` from the POST /contributions body reaches `eval()` unsanitized at line 33, with validation only applied afterwards at line 47.",
"impact": "Any authenticated user can execute arbitrary JavaScript on the server by setting afterTax to a malicious expression, achieving remote code execution.",
"fix": "Replace eval(req.body.afterTax) with Number(req.body.afterTax) or parseInt(req.body.afterTax, 10) plus a NaN check before use.",
"title": "Server-side JavaScript injection via eval() on contribution percentage (roth)",

"evidence": "Same handler and route as the preTax/afterTax findings: `req.body.roth` from the POST /contributions body reaches `eval()` unsanitized at line 34, with validation only applied afterwards at line 47.",
"impact": "Any authenticated user can execute arbitrary JavaScript on the server by setting roth to a malicious expression, achieving remote code execution.",
"fix": "Replace eval(req.body.roth) with Number(req.body.roth) or parseInt(req.body.roth, 10) plus a NaN check before use.",
"title": "Open redirect via unvalidated url query parameter",

"evidence": "The GET /learn handler (app/routes/index.js:70-73) takes `req.query.url` directly from the request's query string and passes it straight to `res.redirect()` at line 72 with no allowlist, host check or relative-path enforcement; the comment on line 71 itself flags this as the insecure pattern.",

"impact": "An attacker can craft a link such as /learn?url=https://evil.example/phish that, once clicked by a logged-in victim, redirects them from a trusted NodeGoat URL to an attacker-controlled site for phishing or credential harvesting.",
"fix": "Validate the target against an allowlist of known learning-resource hosts/paths, or only allow relative paths within the application, before calling res.redirect().",
"title": "Server-side request forgery via unvalidated url/symbol query parameters",

"evidence": "GET /research is mounted with only isLoggedIn (app/routes/index.js:76). displayResearch (app/routes/research.js:12-34) builds `url` at line 15 by concatenating `req.query.url` and `req.query.symbol` verbatim, both fully attacker-controlled query-string values (the hidden form field in app/views/research.html:17 only pre-fills the default for the browser UI; the server performs no host allowlist or origin check). That `url` is passed unmodified to `needle.get(url, ...)` at line 16, and the fetched response body is written back to the client raw at line 25 (`res.write(body)`).",

"impact": "An authenticated user can set url to an internal or cloud-metadata address (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ or http://localhost:<internal-port>/) and have the server fetch it on their behalf, exfiltrating internal service responses or cloud credentials back through the reflected response body.",

"fix": "Validate and allowlist the destination host (e.g. restrict to finance.yahoo.com) before calling needle.get, resolve and re-check the IP to block private/link-local/metadata ranges, and never let the request supply the full request URL.",
"title": "Stored XSS: unescaped markdown-rendered memo output with autoescape disabled",

"evidence": "addMemos (app/routes/memos.js:11-17) stores `req.body.memo` verbatim via memosDAO.insert with no HTML sanitization (app/data/memos-dao.js:15-23). displayMemos (app/routes/memos.js:19-33) fetches all stored memos and renders the `memos` template; app/views/memos.html:31 outputs `marked(doc.memo)` through the swig `{{ }}` expression. server.js:135-142 sets `swig.setDefaults({ autoescape: false })` globally, so swig performs no HTML escaping on this output, and marked()'s own `sanitize: true` option (server.js:126-128) is the only remaining defense, which is a known-bypassable, deprecated safeguard in marked 0.3.5.",

"impact": "Any logged-in user can submit a memo containing HTML/script content (e.g. via a markdown construct marked's sanitizer fails to strip, or raw HTML since sanitize is not a full parser-level guarantee) that executes in every other user's browser when they view /memos, enabling session/cookie theft or actions performed as another user.",

"fix": "Re-enable swig's default autoescaping (remove autoescape: false in server.js) and, for the deliberately-raw markdown output, sanitize the rendered HTML with an allowlist library (e.g. DOMPurify server-side) immediately before rendering rather than relying on marked's sanitize option alone.",
"title": "Reflected XSS: unescaped firstName echoed into input value attribute",
"snippet": "<input type=\"text\" class=\"form-control\" id=\"firstName\" name=\"firstName\" value=\"{{firstNameSafeString}}\" placeholder=\"Enter first name\">",

"evidence": "handleProfileUpdate (app/routes/profile.js:40-107) validates only bankRouting; when that regex fails, line 64 sets `const firstNameSafeString = firstName;` directly from `req.body.firstName` with no encoding, and renders it back via res.render(\"profile\", {..., firstNameSafeString, ...}) at line 65. app/views/profile.html:41 places `{{firstNameSafeString}}` inside the value attribute; swig's global `autoescape: false` (server.js:137) means no HTML-entity encoding is applied.",

"impact": "A user can submit firstName containing `\"><script>...</script>` in a POST /profile request with an intentionally-invalid bankRouting value, breaking out of the value attribute and executing arbitrary script in their own (or, if combined with another stored path, another user's) browser session.",

"fix": "Enable swig's default autoescaping, or explicitly HTML-attribute-encode firstName (e.g. via node-esapi's encodeForHTMLAttribute, matching the pattern already used for `website` at profile.js:28) before assigning it to firstNameSafeString.",
"title": "Reflected XSS: unescaped firstName echoed into href attribute (javascript: URI)",
"snippet": "Google search this profile by name",

"evidence": "Same source as the sibling finding: `firstNameSafeString` is `req.body.firstName` unencoded (app/routes/profile.js:42-64). app/views/profile.html:78 places it inside an href attribute with swig autoescape disabled (server.js:137). The file's own comment at lines 76-77 flags that this is the wrong encoding context for a URL.",

"impact": "A user can set firstName to `javascript:alert(document.cookie)` so that clicking the rendered 'Google search this profile by name' link executes arbitrary script in the victim's browser session, since the value lands directly in an href with no URL-context encoding or scheme allowlist.",

"fix": "HTML/URL-encode firstName for this specific context (e.g. ESAPI.encoder().encodeForURL(...) into a separate firstNameSafeURLString field, as the code's own TODO at profile.js:29-31 describes) and reject non-http(s) schemes before placing any value in an href.",

The result: every response leaves this server with no Content-Security-Policy, no X-Frame-Options, no X-Content-Type-Options, no Strict-Transport-Security, and the default `X-Powered-By: Express` fingerprint intact.", 13: "impact": "Clickjacking (no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options), unrestricted script/style sources for any injected content (no CSP), MIME-type confusion attacks (no X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff), no forced HTTPS upgrade (no HSTS), and easy fingerprinting of the framework/version via X-Powered-By to target known Express/Node CVEs.", 14: "fix": "Require and mount helmet() as the first middleware in the stack, before favicon/body-parser/session: `app.use(helmet());` plus an explicit `contentSecurityPolicy` policy, `app.disable(\"x-powered-by\")`, and `helmet.hsts()` once the app is served over HTTPS.", 15: "references": ["https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html", "https://owasp.org/Top10/A05_2021-Security_Misconfiguration/", "https://helmetjs.github.io/"] 16: }, 17: { 18: "id": "platform-session-cookie-flags", 19: "cwe": "CWE-614", 20: "owasp": "A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration", 21: "severity": "high", 22: "confidence": "confirmed", 23: "title": "Session cookie is issued without Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, an explicit name, or an expiry", 24: "file": "server.js", 25: "line": 78, 26: "snippet": "app.use(session({", 27: "evidence": "The express-session options object at lines 78-102 sets only `secret`, `saveUninitialized: true` and `resave: true`. lines.text: "title": "No security response headers are set anywhere in the middleware stack",

"evidence": "server.js is read end to end: line 10 shows `const helmet = require(\"helmet\");` commented out, and the whole block at lines 38-65 (app.disable(\"x-powered-by\"), helmet.frameguard(), helmet.noCache(), helmet.contentSecurityPolicy(), helmet.hsts(), nosniff()) is inside a `/* ... */` comment, never executed. The first middleware that actually runs is `app.use(favicon(...))` at line 68, followed by body-parser (71-75), express-session (78-102) and the route table (132), none of which set any response header. package.json lists \"helmet\": \"^2.0.0\" as a dependency, so it is installed but never mounted. The result: every response leaves this server with no Content-Security-Policy, no X-Frame-Options, no X-Content-Type-Options, no Strict-Transport-Security, and the default `X-Powered-By: Express` fingerprint intact.",

"impact": "Clickjacking (no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options), unrestricted script/style sources for any injected content (no CSP), MIME-type confusion attacks (no X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff), no forced HTTPS upgrade (no HSTS), and easy fingerprinting of the framework/version via X-Powered-By to target known Express/Node CVEs.",

"fix": "Require and mount helmet() as the first middleware in the stack, before favicon/body-parser/session: `app.use(helmet());` plus an explicit `contentSecurityPolicy` policy, `app.disable(\"x-powered-by\")`, and `helmet.hsts()` once the app is served over HTTPS.",
"title": "Session cookie is issued without Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, an explicit name, or an expiry",

"evidence": "The express-session options object at lines 78-102 sets only `secret`, `saveUninitialized: true` and `resave: true`. The `cookie` option that would set `httpOnly`/`secure`/`maxAge` is present only inside a `/* ... */` comment at lines 92-100 (`cookie: { httpOnly: true /* secure: true */ }`), and the `key: \"sessionId\"` override that would replace the default cookie name is likewise commented out at lines 86-90. With no `cookie` object, express-session falls back to its defaults: the cookie is named `connect.sid`, has no `Secure` flag, no `HttpOnly` flag, no `SameSite` attribute and no `maxAge` (session cookie only, but still readable by any script for the life of the tab).",

"impact": "Because the cookie is not HttpOnly, any script-injection point in the app (this codebase also disables template auto-escaping globally, see server.js:137) can read `document.cookie` and exfiltrate the session id. Because it is not Secure, the id can be captured on any accidental plain-HTTP request (the app itself listens on plain HTTP only, server.js:145). The default `connect.sid` name confirms to an attacker that this is an Express/express-session app, narrowing the attack surface search.",

"fix": "Set `cookie: { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: \"strict\", maxAge: <bounded value> }` and an explicit non-default `key` (e.g. `key: \"sessionId\"`) on the express-session options, and serve the app over HTTPS so `secure: true` is effective.",
"title": "Login and signup routes have no rate limiting or lockout",

"evidence": "server.js's middleware stack (read end to end) contains only favicon, body-parser and session middleware before the routes are registered (routes(app, db) at server.js:132) — no rate limiter of any kind is mounted globally. `package.json` has no `express-rate-limit` or similar dependency, and a repo-wide search for `rate-limit`/`rateLimit` returns no matches. `handleLoginRequest` in app/routes/session.js (lines 53-119) calls `userDAO.validateLogin` on every POST with no attempt counter, delay, CAPTCHA, or account lockout, so the route at index.js:34 accepts unlimited login attempts.",

"impact": "An attacker can script unlimited username/password guesses against /login (and account-enumeration or spam signups against /signup at index.js:38) at whatever rate the network allows, making credential stuffing and brute force practical against any account.",

"fix": "Mount a limiter (e.g. express-rate-limit) keyed by IP and by username/account on /login, /signup, and any password-reset route, with a lockout or exponential backoff after repeated failures.",
"title": "Global error handler renders the raw error object into the HTML response with auto-escaping disabled",

"evidence": "app/routes/error.js's errorHandler (lines 3-13) logs `err.message`/`err.stack` to the server console and then calls `res.render(\"error-template\", { error: err })`, passing the full Error object (not a sanitized message) as a template variable. app/views/error-template.html line 11 prints that value directly as `{{error}}`. server.js line 137 disables swig's global auto-escaping (`autoescape: false`), so whatever `err.toString()`/coercion produces (framework/driver error text, e.g. a MongoDB error message) is written into the response body unescaped and unfiltered.",

"impact": "Any unhandled error anywhere in the request pipeline (DB errors, thrown exceptions from route handlers) is echoed to the client, leaking internal error text (library names, query context, file paths) that helps an attacker map the backend, and — because auto-escaping is off — any HTML/script characters the error text happens to contain would also be rendered unescaped.",

"fix": "In errorHandler, render only a generic message and a correlation id to the client (`res.render(\"error-template\", { error: \"Something went wrong. Reference: \" + reqId })`), keep the full message/stack in server-side logs only, and re-enable swig auto-escaping.",
"title": "The /learn route redirects to an attacker-controlled URL taken straight from the query string",

"evidence": "The handler at app/routes/index.js:70-73 takes `req.query.url` — fully attacker-controlled — and passes it directly to `res.redirect()` with no allowlist, same-origin check, or validation. The comment on line 71 (\"Insecure way to handle redirects by taking redirect url from query string\") confirms this is unmitigated in the code as written; there is no sanitizer or guard between the source (the query string) and the sink (`res.redirect`).",

"impact": "An attacker can craft a link such as `https://<host>/learn?url=https://evil.example` hosted on the trusted domain; because the route requires only `isLoggedIn`, a logged-in user who clicks it is bounced to an attacker-controlled site, useful for phishing or OAuth-token theft that relies on the victim trusting the redirecting domain.",

"fix": "Validate `req.query.url` against an allowlist of known-safe destinations (or require it to be a path on the same origin) before calling res.redirect(); reject or default to a fixed page otherwise.",
"title": "Full application config, including the session cookie secret and crypto key, is dumped to stdout on every start, and the environment defaults to development",

"evidence": "config/config.js line 5 defaults `finalEnv` to `\"development\"` when NODE_ENV is unset (`process.env.NODE_ENV || \"development\"`), and config/env/production.js (read in full) is an empty `module.exports = {}` — it adds no production-specific hardening over the defaults in config/env/all.js. Lines 12-13 then unconditionally `console.log` the fully merged config object via `util.inspect`, which includes `cookieSecret: \"session_cookie_secret_key_here\"` and `cryptoKey: \"a_secure_key_for_crypto_here\"` from config/env/all.js (lines 8-9) — this runs on every process start in every environment, including a misconfigured production deploy, with no guard on NODE_ENV.",

"impact": "Whatever captures process stdout (container logs, a log aggregator, a CI job's console output) gets a full copy of the session-signing secret and the crypto key on every restart, and a missing/blank NODE_ENV silently keeps the app in its least-hardened, development-oriented configuration rather than failing closed.",

"fix": "Remove the unconditional console.log of the full config object (or redact secret-bearing keys before logging), and fail startup if NODE_ENV is not explicitly set to a known value rather than silently defaulting to \"development\".",

"impact": "The session-signing secret and encryption key are written in full to the process's standard output on every start, so anyone with access to container logs, a process manager's log file (Procfile/forever), or a centralized log aggregator that captures stdout gets both secrets even if the source values were later rotated to be environment-supplied.",
"fix": "Remove this debug dump, or redact known-sensitive keys (`cookieSecret`, `cryptoKey`) before logging, and never log a fully merged config object at info level.",
"title": "A hard-coded AES/PBKDF2 key is committed in default configuration, though the code that would consume it is currently commented out",

"evidence": "This literal is exported alongside `cryptoAlgo: \"aes256\"`. The only consumers I found are app/data/profile-dao.js lines 15-40, which define `createIV`/`encrypt`/`decrypt` using `config.cryptoKey`, but that entire block sits inside a `/* Fix for A6 ... */` comment, and the active (uncommented) `updateUser`/`getByUserId` code stores `ssn`/`dob` in plaintext without calling encrypt/decrypt. The only other reference is app/views/tutorial/a6.html, itself example/tutorial markup, not executed application code.",

"impact": "The key is not reachable through any currently active code path I found, so it does not protect live data today; however it is a real secret sitting in version control, and re-enabling the commented Fix-for-A6 block (the documented intended fix) would immediately put a publicly known key into production use for encrypting SSNs and dates of birth.",

"fix": "If encryption is enabled, source the key from a secrets manager or environment variable rather than this file, and rotate this literal since it has already been published; otherwise remove the dead key/config field entirely.",
"title": "An RSA private key is committed to the repository and referenced by a commented-out HTTPS listener",

"evidence": "server.js lines 21-28 (inside a comment block titled \"Fix for A6-Sensitive Data Exposure\") read this exact file via `fs.readFileSync(path.resolve(__dirname, \"./artifacts/cert/server.key\"))` to build `httpsOptions`, and lines 149-155 (also commented) would start `https.createServer(httpsOptions, app)`. The active code only starts a plain `http.createServer(app)` at line 145, so this key is not loaded by the app as shipped.",

"impact": "The private key half of the server's TLS certificate is published in source control. It is currently unused because the HTTPS listener is commented out, but anyone who has cloned the repository already holds the key; if an operator re-enables the commented HTTPS block without replacing the key/cert pair, every clone of this repository could decrypt or MITM TLS traffic to that server.",

"fix": "Never ship a private key in the repository, commented-out code path or not; generate certificates per deployment (or via ACME/Let's Encrypt) and load them from a mounted secret, and rotate/revoke this key since it has already been published.",
"title": "OWASP ZAP proxy API key for local security-scan tooling is hard-coded in the development config",

"evidence": "This literal, together with `zapHostName: \"192.168.56.20\"` and `zapPort: \"8080\"` on lines 3-4, is read by test/security/profile-test.js (`var zapApiKey = config.zapApiKey;` at line 28) and passed to the `zaproxy` client to drive the local ZAP security-regression test suite against a private-range IP. The identical literal is also committed in config/env/test.js line 6.",

"impact": "This key only authenticates to a local OWASP ZAP proxy instance on a private/lab IP address used for the project's own security regression tests; it is not a production application credential and is not reachable by a remote attacker over the internet. It is still a committed secret and, if that lab host were ever reachable, would let an attacker drive the ZAP proxy's API.",
"fix": "Move the ZAP API key to an environment variable read only by the test harness, and rotate it since it is public; do not ship it as a JS literal even for internal tooling.",
"title": "Cypress e2e fixture repeats the seeded admin password in plaintext",

"evidence": "This fixture is loaded by the Cypress end-to-end suite (test/e2e/integration/login_spec.js and others) to log in as the seeded admin account during tests.
